# A sharp-capacity midpoint-centroid counterexample in every continuous dimension

This is an exact obstruction to one proposed three-fiber selection rule.
It is not an OC counterexample. It strengthens the interval and rectangle
examples in `candidate 25b281541ed968f0`:
the midpoint-density capacity here is attained exactly for EVERY d>=1,
and the resulting candidate fails its OC depth threshold in EVERY d>=1.

## 1. Actual nonheavy homothetic simplex fibers

Fix d>=1. Let T={x>=0:sum x_i<=1}, V=|T|=1/d!, and let g be its
centroid, whose coordinates all equal 1/(d+1). Write

    epsilon=1/10, a=epsilon^d, r=(1+epsilon)/2=11/20,
    Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d.

At integer bases -1,0,+1 take respectively

    A=epsilon T, B=T, C=T.

Their lifted convex hull is a full-dimensional compact convex body with
exactly those integer fibers. Indeed (A+C)/2=rT subset B, so the middle
fiber is unchanged by taking that hull. All three fiber volumes are
positive. The total mixed volume is M=(2+a)V, and each of aV,V,V is
strictly below M/2. Thus no heavy-fiber exception is present.

The exact midpoint capacity supplied by ordinary Brunn--Minkowski is

    s=((|A|^(1/d)+|C|^(1/d))/2)^d=r^d V=|rT|.

It is the actual midpoint volume, not merely a lower bound.

## 2. The proposed full-target density centroid

The positive affine transport x -> x/epsilon sends the uniform law of A
to that of C. Its midpoint map sends the uniform law of A to the uniform
law of D=rT. Hence the mass-|A| midpoint measure is

    eta=(a/r^d)1_D dx.

It has mass aV and attains the sharp density upper bound |A|/s exactly.
Its support lies in B. A different midpoint coupling satisfying that
same sharp density bound must give the same eta: its support is contained
in D and the density upper bound already integrates to its entire mass.
Even without this saturation observation, its mean is fixed by the two
uniform endpoint marginals.

The proposed full-target multiplier and candidate are

    L=(|A|+|C|)/|A|=(1+a)/a,
    y=(0,hg),
    h=[1+(1+a)r]/(2+a)=(31+11a)/(40+20a).

The measure 1_B dx+L eta has total mass M, and the displayed point is
exactly its centroid placed on the middle integer fiber. It belongs to
that fiber since 0<h<1. This is a deterministic admissible candidate;
its failure below is a depth failure, not an inadmissible base.

## 3. A strict oblique cap defeats that candidate

Put c=d/(d+1), q=ch, and take the closed ambient halfspace

    H={(z,x):sum_i x_i+z<=q}.

It passes through y. On base -1, its threshold for sum x_i is q+1,
strictly larger than epsilon, so it captures all of A. On base +1,
its threshold is q-1<0, so it strictly excludes C. Its middle trace is
qT. Consequently its exact mass is

    mu(H)/V=q^d+a=Gamma h^d+a.                         (1)

For every a>0, direct cross multiplication gives h<=31/40. Also c>=1/2,
so a/Gamma=(epsilon/c)^d<=(1/5)^d. Therefore

    mu(H)/(Gamma V)
       <=(31/40)^d+(1/5)^d
       <=31/40+1/5=39/40
       <1+a/2=M/(2V).                                (2)

Here x^d<=x for 0<x<1 and integer d>=1 proves the second inequality.
Equations (1)-(2) give the exact strict failure

    mu(H)<(Gamma/2)M.

All endpoint traces are strictly full or empty, and the middle boundary
has zero d-volume. The normal genuinely couples the integer and
continuous coordinates. Its mass is the actual original source mass,
including all endpoint payment, not only a lower relaxation through eta.

The proposed auxiliary source-cost inequality also fails. For the middle
trace H_0, the pointwise midpoint indicator inequality gives

    |B intersect H_0|+eta(H_0)<=mu(H)<(Gamma/2)M.

Thus density-capacity saturation, exact full-target mass, nonheavy fibers,
and an admissible selected point are jointly insufficient for this rule.

## 4. A separate safe center; no OC counterexample

The completed measurable-subset payment in
`candidate bb74919333cc624f`, Section 8, applies
to E,K,K at bases -1,0,1 whenever E subset K. At the ordinary centroid
of the middle K it gives, for every containing ambient halfspace,

    mass >= Gamma_d |K|+lambda_d |E|,
    lambda_1=1,
    lambda_d=[(2d/(d+1))^(d/(d-1))-1]^(d-1)>1/2 (d>=2).

This is an already proved ordinary tail inequality and actual three-source
payment, not a use of unrestricted OC. Taking E=epsilon T and K=T gives
at (0,g) the lower bound (Gamma+lambda_d a)V. Since Gamma<=1/2,
lambda_d>Gamma/2 in every case, so this is strictly greater than
(Gamma/2)M. Vertical caps are also covered directly: each contains the
whole middle T, while (Gamma/2)(2+a)<1.

Accordingly the own-middle centroid is safe and the proposed centroid
of B+L eta is not. The conclusions concern this precise selection rule;
neither the sharp midpoint-density theorem nor OC is disproved.
